title: real-app-discovery-lab
universal_lens: Real App Discovery Lab operationalizes launch validation through kill, merge, fix, build, polish, measure, teach, surprise. These actions define a causal lattice of evidence-based app readiness, where each primitive maps to a state transition in GSE and a probabilistic update in GSI.
gsi_mapping: GSI models launch readiness as a conformal predictive process over app states. Each kill, merge, and polish action updates belief distributions over live vs. draft app surfaces using Bayesian evidence layers from API health and compliance signals.
gse_mapping: GSE encodes discovery as a finite-state automaton with transitions driven by runtime validation. The kill and merge primitives define safe launch boundaries; fix and build actions resolve state inconsistencies; polish and teach refine user interaction models.

primitives.name: Launch Claim Nullifier
primitives.verbatim_quote: Kill - Kill any launch claim that implies Player Lab or roster-current intelligence is live until the app exposes and validates that surface.
primitives.assumptions: Launch claims are false unless validated by runtime API surface.
primitives.breakdown_regime: L = 1 when V = 0, L = 0 when V = 1.

layer2.mapping: GSI belief update P(L=1|V=0) → 1, P(L=1|V=1) → 0; GSE state transition from draft to live.
layer2.telemetry: API surface exposure and compliance status

primitives.name: Evidence Layer Integrator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Merge - Merge docs-only launch packets into this real-app evidence layer.
primitives.assumptions: Docs-only evidence must be merged with runtime validation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: E_r = 1 ⇒ E_d is integrated into E_r.

layer2.mapping: GSI combines prior docs with posterior runtime data; GSE merges static and dynamic app state.

primitives.name: User Surface Refinement
primitives.verbatim_quote: Polish - Pricing, promotions, methodology, brief, and picks after critical runtime fixes.
primitives.assumptions: Surface refinement occurs only after functional integrity is verified.

layer2.mapping: GSI refines user belief models via surface consistency; GSE applies UI polish post-failure resolution.
layer2.telemetry: User engagement metrics on polished surfaces

primitives.name: Autopsy Risk Modeler
primitives.verbatim_quote: Surprise - Weekly autopsy receipts that explain what changed and what the model learned without exposing method.
primitives.assumptions: Risk changes are modeled without revealing internal logic.
primitives.breakdown_regime: R = g(M), M increases ⇒ R shifts.

layer2.mapping: GSI learns risk dynamics through retrospective analysis; GSE adjusts failure modes based on learned patterns.

'Merge' integrates static documentation with dynamic evidence, forming a Bayesian belief layer. 'Polish' refines surfaces only after functional fixes, aligning with GSE's state machine. 'Surprise' introduces retroactive risk modeling, enabling GSI to learn from failure modes without leaking internal structure. These operators define a dual system: GSE handles operational transitions, while GSI governs probabilistic belief updates. Each primitive is a logical gate in a larger system of launch validation, where failure modes are detected and corrected before live exposure. The interplay between these primitives ensures that neither GSE nor GSI operates in isolation but rather in a tightly coupled feedback loop of evidence, belief, and action.
